name: Effective Maximum-Parent Profile from One Parent
statement: Given a nonempty proper finite class and one maximum parent with profile $(r_0,s_0)$, a finite procedure computes every coordinatewise minimal point of $\mathcal F(C)$ and a parent certificate for each. It therefore computes the least parent rank, least complementary rank, and least auxiliary count.
proof: The profile is upward closed by nested maximum lifts, and its minimal points form a finite antichain. Use the fixed-rank auxiliary bound to decide and find the least feasible point in every row $r<r_0$. Apply the same procedure to the complement to find the least point in every column $s<s_0$. Add the supplied point and discard dominated entries. Any other minimal point must lie in one of those rows or columns, because otherwise the supplied point dominates it.
comments: This is a termination theorem, not an efficiency bound. Without one supplied feasible parent it does not decide unrestricted nonmembership.
